Changelog
Jules Turndown
October 29, 2026
We’re writing to let you know that as part of our work to unify our agentic coding efforts, Jules will wind down on December 31, 2026. You have until November 11, 2026 to continue finishing up sessions. After November 11, 2026, we will be turning Jules to read-only until the end of the year.

When we launched Jules, it was an experiment to learn how asynchronous coding agents could help you tackle your backlog and ship faster. What you built with it taught us where agentic development is headed, and those learnings are shaping products across Google, including our agent-first platform, Google Antigravity.

You can now export everything Jules knows about your work into a local folder: account settings, environment variables, scheduled tasks, connected repositories, memories, setup scripts, and every session, including its prompt, plan, full activity log, and code patches.

Your code, branches, and pull requests already live in GitHub, so they stay where they are. The export covers the configuration and history that live inside Jules.

To export, install Jules Tools and sign in:

npm install -g @google/jules
jules login

Then open a CLI coding agent, such as Claude Code, from your home directory and paste the export prompt below. The agent checks your setup, runs the export, and tells you what it saved.

steps: Check and set up Jules CLI environment and verify login credentials.
If authentication credentials are not found, prompt the user to run `! jules login` and await confirmation.
Verify repository connection via `jules remote list --repo`.
Save the export script to `/home/jules/export_jules.py` and execute it from `/home/jules`.
Output the export results (counts and path) while ensuring tokens and env variables remain private.
Complete pre-commit steps to ensure proper testing, verification, review, and reflection are done.
Finalize and report export details to the user.
